title: Getting started
intro: Touchdown keeps the flights you have flown and the aircraft you have photographed, and works out statistics from them. These are the first steps.
modes.title: Modes
modes.browser: Your log is always in this browser. Standard and Private also keep it in storage you own, so your other devices sync with it.
modes.difference: The difference is who can open that copy. In Standard, Touchdown's server can, so it can show the links you share and you connect Google Drive only once. In Private, only your own browsers can.
modes.selected: You selected {mode} mode. Change it in Settings, under Sync mode.
modes.figure.kept.standard: In this browser and your Google Drive
modes.figure.kept.private: In this browser and your Google Drive or a directory
modes.figure.server: Touchdown's server can open your log
myfr24.title: Your flights from myFR24
myfr24.export: On my.flightradar24.com, open Settings › Export and download the CSV file.
myfr24.import: Open <link>Import</link> here and choose the file. Every row is checked before anything is saved.
myfr24.review: Look through what the checks found, then import. An import can be undone.
spreadsheet.title: A spreadsheet
spreadsheet.layout: A flight or spotting log kept in a spreadsheet comes in through Import too, as a CSV or Excel file, in any layout.
spreadsheet.columns: Import works out which column holds what, and asks about the columns it is unsure of.
add.title: Adding flights and sightings
add.button: Use the + button at the top of every page.
add.flight: A <link>flight</link> needs its flight number and date first. The rest is optional.
add.session: A <link>spotting session</link> takes the day and the airport once, then one registration after another.
add.figure.session.sub: Day and airport once, then registrations
tracks.title: Recorded tracks
tracks.greatCircle: A flight is drawn, and measured, as the great circle between its airports until it has a recorded track. Then its distance is the one flown.
tracks.fr24: With a Flightradar24 subscription, download a flight's track as CSV or KML and add it on the flight's page, under Add track.
tracks.missing: The Flights page lists the flights without one, as a file to send to someone who can find them.
tracks.figure.greatCircle: Great circle, until a track is added
issues.title: Issues
issues.list: <link>Issues</link> lists what looks wrong in the log, such as a registration that does not fit its aircraft type or times out of order.
issues.fix: Use the fix it suggests. A warning that is right as it is can be marked “This is right”.
issues.figure.fix: Move takeoff and landing to the next day ({date})
sharing.title: Sharing
sharing.how: Share, on a flight’s, a sighting’s or an aircraft’s page, on Flights and on Home, sends an image or a video of its map in every mode, and in Standard mode makes a link. Shared links, in the menu at the top, lists the links.
sharing.anyone: Anyone with a link can open it, read only, until you stop it.
sharing.preview: Pasted into a chat app, a link shows a preview: its title and a picture of its map.
sharing.private: Ticket numbers and booking references are never in a link.
sharing.figure.private: Ticket numbers and booking references stay out
sharing.figure.preview: Chat apps show a preview of its map
sharing.figure.files: Or an image or a video of its map, in every mode
export.title: Taking your log elsewhere
export.text: <link>Settings</link>, under Data, makes a backup of everything, each table as CSV, a Google Sheet with a tab for each table, and a file of your flights for myFR24's import. In Standard and Private mode, Touchdown also keeps daily copies of your log in your storage, listed there too.
